# Slicer MCP tools: profile `ct_segments` (model-facing reference)

- Tool schema version: `slicer-mcp-tools-v1`
- Protocol config: `ct-segments-v1`, sha256 `16e7075b62b5`
- Report: `json-object-v1` (built in; a harness passes its own with `serve --report`)
- Segmentation: liver, spleen, kidney_left, kidney_right, aorta, pancreas

Descriptions, instructions and schemas below are exactly what the MCP server sends to the model.

## Overview

| Tools (model) | Runner-only | Live views | Bridge state keys (traced) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | `reset_episode`, `end_episode`, `observe` | 3d, axial, sagittal, coronal | `case_loaded`, `camera`, `render`, `clip`, `slices`, `focus_ras`, `wl`, `segments (a profile with a segmentation)`, `slice_tools` |

Runner-only tools carry the tool `_meta` `{"slicer_mcp/runner_only": true}`; the client must hide them from the model.

## Result format

Every call returns MCP content: `content[0]` is one text block holding the JSON object `{step_index, state, result, warnings, error, frames}`; `content[1:]` are the images named in `frames`, in that order, each a PNG of 512 x 512 pixels. `state` is the bridge state as is (the trace keeps the same); `result` holds the tool's own output; `warnings` lists every clamp (`name=v clamped to c (allowed [lo, hi])`) and edge stop. On any error `is_error` is true, the JSON has the same shape, and `error` is `{type, message}`.

### Error types

| error.type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `invalid_argument` | the model's fault (bad arguments, a tool outside the profile, an invalid report, a call after the report); logged as a step, nothing changes, the episode continues |
| `not_found` | the bridge could not find what the call named; logged as a step, the episode continues |
| `no_episode` | no episode is running (the runner must call reset_episode first) |
| `episode_closed` | the episode has ended (report submitted); no further calls are accepted |
| `environment` | bridge internal or connection error; the runner should abort the episode |
| `stale_render` | internal (EnvSession, logged in the trace): a frozen frame, i.e. byte-identical to the view's previous frame while its state changed; the model-facing type is `environment`, so the runner aborts |
| `identity_mismatch` | internal (EnvSession, logged in the trace): the bridge answered for another episode or another loaded volume; the model-facing type is `environment`, so the runner aborts |

## Server instructions

```text
CT viewer with segmented structures.

How the tools work
- Coordinates are RAS (patient Right, Anterior, Superior) in millimetres; angles in degrees.
- Every tool returns one JSON text block {step_index, state, result, warnings, error, frames} followed by the images named in frames, in that order.
- Out-of-range numbers are clamped and reported in warnings; invalid arguments return an error and change nothing.
- Each tool's description gives its arguments, defaults, limits and refusals.
```

## Tools

### `reset_episode` (runner only)

- title: Reset episode (runner only)
- read-only: no
- runner-only: yes
- returns frames: every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: runner only: load the case, restore the deterministic initial view, start a new trace (step 0); an open episode is closed as abandoned

Description:

```text
RUNNER ONLY: never offer this tool to the model. Loads the anonymised case, brings the viewer to its deterministic initial state and starts a new episode and trace (step 0). An open episode is closed as abandoned. client_meta (model_id, model_version, system_prompt_sha256, seed, ...) goes to meta.json. Returns the 3D view and the axial, sagittal and coronal slice views at the initial view, and the volume geometry in result.case_info: voxel dimensions and spacing (mm), RAS bounds (mm), the centre point, and each slice view's position range (axial along S, sagittal along R, coronal along A). With segments (a profile with a segmentation): also loads the case's segmentation shells; case_info.segments lists the structures and their colours.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `case_id` | string | yes | length 1 .. 64; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}$` |  |  | anonymised case id |
| `client_meta` | object or null | no |  |  | `null` | episode metadata for meta.json: model_id, model_version, system_prompt_sha256, seed, and anything else |

### `set_slice`

- title: Set slice position
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: the slice view named by `view`; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: RAS coordinate along the view axis (axial->S, sagittal->R, coronal->A), clamped to the volume; slab_mm = a maximum-intensity slab, kept until set to 0

Description:

```text
Move one slice view to a position in mm along its own axis, in patient (RAS) coordinates: axial -> S (larger = more superior), sagittal -> R (larger = further to the patient's right), coronal -> A (larger = more anterior). The position is clamped to the volume (ranges in the reset result's case_info). slab_mm (0 to 20) turns the view into a maximum-intensity slab of that thickness: each pixel shows the brightest value through the slab. The slab stays on that view while you scroll or move it, until you set slab_mm 0; omit slab_mm to keep it as it is. Returns that slice view.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | yes |  | `axial`, `sagittal`, `coronal` |  | slice view: axial (position along S), sagittal (R) or coronal (A) |
| `position_mm` | number | yes |  |  |  | position in mm along the view's axis (RAS coordinate); clamped to the volume |
| `slab_mm` | number or null | no |  |  | `null` | thickness in mm of a maximum-intensity slab through the view (0 = an ordinary thin slice); kept while scrolling |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `scroll_slice`

- title: Scroll slice
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: the slice view named by `view`; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: whole slices; stops at the volume edge (warning)

Description:

```text
Scroll one slice view by a whole number of slices (positive = towards S / R / A; one slice = the view's slice spacing). At most +-200 slices per call (clamped). The scroll stops at the volume edge, with a warning. Returns that slice view and how far it moved (moved_slices, moved_mm).
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | yes |  | `axial`, `sagittal`, `coronal` |  | slice view: axial (position along S), sagittal (R) or coronal (A) |
| `delta_slices` | integer | yes | -200 .. 200 |  |  | whole slices to move (+ = towards S / R / A); clamped to +-200 |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `jump_to_point`

- title: Jump slices to point
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: axial, sagittal, coronal; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: all three slices through the point (clamped to the voxel-centre range); sets the focus; result.hu (mean HU in a small ball)

Description:

```text
Move all three slice views through a point [R, A, S] in mm: sagittal takes R, coronal takes A, axial takes S. Each coordinate is clamped to the volume. The point becomes the focus (where the three slice views cross). result.inside_segment names the structure (liver, spleen, kidney_left, kidney_right, aorta, pancreas) whose segmented blood pool contains the point, or null. result.hu is the mean CT value (HU) within 1 mm of the point. While the slices are zoomed (zoom view slices), every slice view is re-centred on the new focus, so point at the new frames. Returns the three slice views.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ras` | number[3] | yes |  |  |  | point [R, A, S] in mm (patient coordinates; geometry in the reset result's case_info) |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `point_at`

- title: Point at pixel
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: axial, sagittal, coronal; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: the other two slices through the pixel's RAS point; sets the focus; result.hu (mean HU in a small ball)

Description:

```text
Point at a pixel of a slice view's most recent image: view, then x (column, 0 = left edge) and y (row, 0 = top edge), in that image's pixels (0 to 511). The pixel's patient position becomes the focus: the other two slice views move through it, and the view you pointed at stays where it is. result.ras is the point [R, A, S] in mm. result.inside_segment names the structure (liver, spleen, kidney_left, kidney_right, aorta, pancreas) whose segmented blood pool contains the point, or null. result.hu is the mean CT value (HU) within 1 mm of the point. While the slices are zoomed (zoom view slices), every slice view is re-centred on the new focus, so point at the new frames. pan_to and set_clip_box use the focus when you give them no point. Returns the three slice views.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | yes |  | `axial`, `sagittal`, `coronal` |  | slice view: axial (position along S), sagittal (R) or coronal (A) |
| `x` | number | yes | 0 .. 511 |  |  | pixel column in that view's last frame (0 = left edge) |
| `y` | number | yes | 0 .. 511 |  |  | pixel row in that view's last frame (0 = top edge) |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `orbit`

- title: Orbit camera
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: 3d; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: trackball about the focal point, relative; from anterior, azimuth +90 -> camera at patient left

Description:

```text
Rotate the 3D camera about its focal point, relative to the current view, in degrees: azimuth about the screen's vertical axis, then elevation about the screen's horizontal axis, then roll about the viewing direction. It is a trackball, so going over the top is fine. From the anterior view, azimuth +90 moves the camera to the patient's left and elevation +90 looks from above. Per call: azimuth +-180, elevation +-90, roll +-180 (clamped). Returns the 3D view.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `azimuth_deg` | number | no | -180 .. 180 |  | `0` | rotation about the screen's vertical axis |
| `elevation_deg` | number | no | -90 .. 90 |  | `0` | rotation about the screen's horizontal axis |
| `roll_deg` | number | no | -180 .. 180 |  | `0` | rotation about the viewing direction |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `zoom`

- title: Zoom
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: 3d; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: relative factor, > 1 = closer; the cumulative zoom is clamped too; view=slices zooms the slice views about the focus, which then follow the focus

Description:

```text
Zoom the 3D view by a factor relative to the current zoom (> 1 = closer, < 1 = farther), 0.25 to 4 per call. The total zoom relative to the initial view stays within [0.25, 4] (clamped, with a warning). Returns the 3D view. With view 'slices' it zooms the three slice views instead, about the focus (where they cross): the total slice zoom stays within [1, 3] (clamped, with a warning), the slice views are re-centred on the focus whenever point_at or jump_to_point moves it (set_slice and scroll_slice do not pan them), and reset_view (or zooming back to 1) shows the whole slice again. Returns the three slice views.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `factor` | number | yes | 0.25 .. 4 |  |  | > 1 zooms in, < 1 zooms out |
| `view` | string or null | no |  |  | `null` | '3d' (default) zooms the 3D view; 'slices' zooms the three slice views about the focus |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `set_clip_box`

- title: Clip to box
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: 3d; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: keeps only the axis-aligned box (default centre: the focus)

Description:

```text
Crop the 3D rendering to an axis-aligned box: keep only what lies inside the box centred at center_ras [R, A, S] with edge lengths size_mm [R, A, S], in mm. Omit center_ras to centre the box on the focus (where the three slice views cross). The centre is clamped to the volume; each size to at least 5 mm and at most twice the volume's extent. One clip at a time: this replaces a clip plane (with a warning). 3D view only; the slice views are not cut. It cuts the structure shells too. Returns the 3D view.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `center_ras` | number[3] or null | no |  |  | `null` | box centre [R, A, S] in mm; omit it to centre the box on the focus (where the three slice views cross) |
| `size_mm` | number[3] | yes |  |  |  | box edge lengths [R, A, S] in mm |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `set_clip_plane`

- title: Clip with plane
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: 3d; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: removes the side (azimuth, elevation) points to; offset > 0 removes less

Description:

```text
Cut away one side of the 3D rendering with a plane. azimuth_deg and elevation_deg name the side that is REMOVED: azimuth 0 = anterior, +90 = patient left, -90 = patient right, +-180 = posterior; elevation +90 = superior, -90 = inferior (tilting the side towards S or I). The plane is perpendicular to that direction, at offset_mm from the volume centre along it: 0 cuts through the centre, a positive offset moves the cut outward (removes less), a negative one inward (removes more). Ranges: azimuth +-180, elevation +-90, offset +-200 mm (clamped). One clip at a time: this replaces a clip box (with a warning). 3D view only. It cuts the structure shells too. Returns the 3D view.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `azimuth_deg` | number | yes | -180 .. 180 |  |  | side to remove: 0 anterior, 90 patient left, -90 patient right, 180 posterior |
| `elevation_deg` | number | yes | -90 .. 90 |  |  | tilt of that side: 90 superior, -90 inferior |
| `offset_mm` | number | yes | -200 .. 200 |  |  | plane distance from the volume centre towards the removed side |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `set_segment_visibility`

- title: Show or hide structures
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: 3d, axial, sagittal, coronal; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: shows / hides structure shells (show first, then hide); unknown or absent names are errors

Description:

```text
Show or hide individual structure shells (liver brown, spleen purple, kidney_left pink, kidney_right light blue, aorta dark red, pancreas yellow). show is applied first, then hide, so show ['all'] with hide ['spleen'] shows everything but spleen; a name in both is an error. Hidden structures disappear from the 3D view and from the slice outlines. Showing a shown structure or hiding a hidden one gives a warning. A name that is not one of liver, spleen, kidney_left, kidney_right, aorta, pancreas, or not segmented in this case (the reset result's case_info.segments lists them), is an error and changes nothing. Returns the 3D view and the three slice views.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | string[] | no | at most 7 items |  | `[]` | structures to show ('all' = every one) |
| `hide` | string[] | no | at most 7 items |  | `[]` | structures to hide ('all' = every one); applied after show |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `center_on_segments`

- title: Centre on structures
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: 3d; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: focal point -> the structures' box centre, zoom to fit it; direction kept

Description:

```text
Centre the 3D view on structures: the focal point moves to the centre of their bounding box and the camera moves along the current viewing direction until the box fills the view (the total zoom is clamped to [0.25, 4], with a warning). names omitted = every shown structure. A name that is not one of liver, spleen, kidney_left, kidney_right, aorta, pancreas, or not segmented in this case (the reset result's case_info.segments lists them), is an error and changes nothing. result.center_ras and result.zoom give the new centre and zoom. Returns the 3D view.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | string[] or null | no | at most 6 items |  | `null` | structures to fit; omit for every shown structure |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |

### `measure`

- title: Measure distance
- read-only: no
- runner-only: no
- returns frames: the slice view named by `view`; with `composite: true`, every view (3d, axial, sagittal, coronal)
- semantics: distance in mm between two pixels of one slice view's last frame; a line without text on that view

Description:

```text
Measure the distance between two pixels of one slice view's most recent image (x1, y1, x2, y2: columns and rows, 0 to 511, as in point_at). result.distance_mm is the distance in mm between their patient positions. A yellow line joins them on that view (it has no text) until the next measure or reset_view; it disappears when the view moves off it. Returns that slice view.
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Bounds | Choices | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | yes |  | `axial`, `sagittal`, `coronal` |  | slice view: axial (position along S), sagittal (R) or coronal (A) |
| `x1` | number | yes | 0 .. 511 |  |  | first point: pixel column in that view's last frame (0 = left edge) |
| `y1` | number | yes | 0 .. 511 |  |  | first point: pixel row (0 = top edge) |
| `x2` | number | yes | 0 .. 511 |  |  | second point: pixel column |
| `y2` | number | yes | 0 .. 511 |  |  | second point: pixel row |
| `composite` | boolean | no |  |  | `false` | also return the frames of all the other views |
